description:
FILED s543b (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-16) while probing #5082.  PRE-EXISTING (base c5f618f2 = the same; filehandles and dirhandles alike).  SILENT WRONG.

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 | PCL):
    open my $f, "<", "/etc/passwd" or die; my $c = $f; close $f;
    open $c, "<", "/etc/hostname" or die;
    print(($c == $f ? "same" : "new"), " ", (defined(fileno $f) ? "f-open" : "f-closed"), "\n");
    # perl: same f-open      PCL: new f-closed
The same for dirhandles: `opendir my $d, D; my $c = $d; closedir $d; opendir $c, D; $c == $d` (perl same, PCL new).

WHAT IT IS: in perl `open my $fh` puts a reference to a GLOB in $fh; a copy `$c = $fh` copies the REFERENCE, and `open $c` re-opens the SAME glob's IO slot -- every holder sees the new stream.  PCL's lexical handle is the stream itself in the box; the opener installs a NEW stream in $c's box only, so $f keeps the closed (or old) stream.  A program that hands a handle to a helper which re-opens it (`reopen($fh)`, `open $_[0], ...` through an alias is fine -- the alias is the same box; a COPY is not) sees the old handle.

DIRECTION (not built): the opener, given a box whose value is a handle (stream/socket/dirhandle record), would have to replace the handle IN PLACE for every holder -- i.e. an indirection object (the glob) shared by the copies, which is the representation question #2056 / #3517 circle (`%p-stream-glob` makes the glob only on demand).  Measure first how often a copy is re-opened in the board / everyday populations.

=== MEASURED, NOT FIXED (s543n, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-24) -- a designed residue, FLAGGED for a ruling ===
HOW OFTEN (scratch/s543n/tools/reopen-census.pl: an open on @_ aliases / on a copied parameter / on a copied
variable / ->open & ->fdopen methods): a COPY of a LEXICAL handle re-opened = 0 in the 30 board dists (1,242 files),
the everyday corpus, perl-tests and perl 5.40.3's 755 core modules; every param-copy open in core is on a GLOB object
(IO::File / IO::Handle / IO::Dir / DirHandle), and the board's 7 `->open` sites are IO::File objects.
WHAT IS RIGHT ALREADY (probe scratch/s543n/probes/pE1.pl, 9 shapes): IO::File `$io->close; $io->open(...)` seen by a
second holder, a Symbol::gensym copy, a `\*FH` copy, a reopen through `$_[0]`, IO::Handle->fdopen on a second holder
-- their holder is a glob, which the opener fills in place.  WRONG: the raw copy (this task), a reopen helper with a
COPIED parameter (`my ($h) = @_; close $h; open $h, ...`), a dirhandle copy, a copy stored in a hash.
WHAT AN IN-PLACE RE-OPEN COSTS: a lexical handle's box holds the SBCL stream itself; a closed fd-stream cannot be
revived or re-pointed (its operations are replaced at close, internals), so every holder seeing a re-open needs an
INDIRECTION shared by the copies -- perl's GV with an IO slot: `open my $fh` would store a glob (a p-typeglob with an
IO slot holding the stream), print / readline resolve box -> glob -> slot (one more memory read per call and a type
dispatch change in %p-resolve-fh's first arm, which #2771 measured at ~6 % of a print loop per extra test), and every
reader that asks `(streamp (p-box-value fh))` today (scope close, the drop flush, fileno, -X, p-ref's GLOB, numeric
identity, bless on a handle, *p-handle-names*, the tie table) moves to the glob.  A representation change for the
reviewing session, not a batch; docs/not-supported.md ns-reopen-through-copy says what holds today.

FREQUENCY (s543n, the USER's ORDINARY-OR-RARE ruling of 2026-11-24): set to `rare` by the measurement above -- the
census also covers the Rosetta corpus (652 programs): 0 re-opens through a copy, 0 `->open` / `->fdopen`.
frequency_reason: MEASURED s543n (scratch/s543n/tools/reopen-census.pl): a re-open through a COPY of a lexical handle occurs 0 times in the 30 board dists (1,242 files), everyday/, perl-tests, the Rosetta corpus (652 programs) and perl 5.40.3's 755 core modules; every param-copy open in core is on a GLOB object (IO::File / IO::Handle / IO::Dir / DirHandle), which PCL already re-opens in place
subject: SILENT WRONG: re-opening a handle through a COPY (`my $c = $fh; close $fh; open $c, ...`) installs a new handle in $c only -- perl re-opens the shared glob ($fh sees it, `$c == $fh`); file and dir handles alike
triage_reason: re-opening a handle through a copy
